item.content:encoded:
What I dig about this is that there are at least three concepts seamlessly rolled into one skip.

You've got the on the surface Phillip K. Dick title turned literal.
Beneath that, the metaphor of clouds in the sky as sheep on a hillside. References some famous poet I vaguely remember from lit class.
But best of all for my money is that the Argonauts/golden fleece lead is completely buried in an absent addendum.

There's probably a fourth angle I don't get hinging on why a ram can be bribed with candy, chewing tobacco, and booze.

item.content:encoded:
These are Pokemon. Specifically, they're Mareep (+ levitation – thunderball tails + horns). Considering that this SCP is a Pokemon, I like how well it's done. I was expecting Mareep and that's almost exactly what I got, but I was impressed by the clinical tone characteristic of the SCP Foundation that allowed me to almost forget that it was a Pokemon. Granted, the fact that it's never specified why SCP-594-1, -2, and -3 are particularly significant was a bit annoying, but maybe it's supposed to be left to the imagination? Overall, I like it.

Also, not all SCP articles have to be horrifying (thankfully). If you tried reading every article on this website - and most of their discussion pages - one by one, in order, back-to-back for a few dozen at a time, you would appreciate the lighter articles, too. ;)

item.title: Electric sheep are actually close than you'd think.
item.content:encoded:
While I may only have joined this site today, I have lurked this site for a while. Not long ago, I cam across how these sheep would exist, without any external (supernatural, human, alien) help.

+ show block
– hide block

Imagine, you are a sheep. Not a very large sheep, mind you, but very, very prone to static. The farmer leaves the gate open, and you escape, along with your herd. You migrate to a nice little valley, and live there. However, the wolves there prey upon the herd, but upon attempting to prey on you, the static discharges into the wolf, scaring it off. The sheep with the most static buildup breed, and eventually, the high static content becomes integrated into the genetic makeup of the herd. Imagine a scenario where every sheep gains the ability to generate mass amounts of electricity, becoming an SCP-594.

How these sheeps would work, would be quite simple. You know how static electricity works, right? You rub against something, and it gets charged. Also, mammals are able to shake their fur, in order to dry off, and remove dirt. These sheep adapted wool that was drastically different than their undercoat, so when they shake, they generate massive amounts of electricity, which is then stored in the wool. This charge is generated, when the normally insulated body of the sheep, rubs against the wool. In function, the shaking of the wool would act like a natural, mammal powered van-de-graff generator.

Through selectively mating, and the trait becoming more and more dominant, the shocks adapt into what these sheep are. Living lightning generators.

However, they have a weakness. Anyone who's worn wet socks, and tried to build up a charge on a carpet knows, that when something is wet, it does not build up a charge. Thus, by discharging, and then dousing the sheep, they'd be unable to build up a charge, until they either shake themselves entirely dry, or sundry.

In fact, humanity as is might end up creating these by accident. Humans already breed sheep based on how fluffy a sheep's wool is, and how much of it there is. If the wool gets too fluffy, electricity will build up… Eventually, someone will think of making electric sheep, and this becomes reality.


In summary, barring levitation, this is closer to reality then thought possible.
